# 本地商户如何应对 AI 搜索

- 作者：Alex Groberman（@alexgroberman）
- 发布时间：2026-10-23 21:15（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/alexgroberman/status/2113620230987776007
- 说明：以下为原帖中文全文翻译，后附英文原文；文中数据和效果为作者表述，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

如果你经营一家本地企业，你现有的网站上就存在一个巨大的 AI 搜索机会。

一项研究分析了超过 20 万次本地 AI 搜索和近 200 万次引用。

结果呢？

AI 系统用作来源的**独立域名**中，93% 是单个企业的网站；企业网站占全部引用的 42%。

因此，尽管人们经常讨论 Reddit、目录网站、评价平台和第三方来源，单个企业的网站在本地 AI 搜索中仍然极其重要。

我们来详细看看。

顺便说一句，如果你想了解自己的企业是否出现在 Google AI、ChatGPT、Claude、Perplexity、Grok 及更广泛的 AI 搜索中，可以从这里开始。免费：

[https://seo-stuff.com/free-audit](https://t.co/Evw8cXXicl)

BrightLocal 分析了涉及 1,342 个商家地点的 200,875 次非品牌本地 AI 搜索，进行了 60 天内的多次检查，并分析了约 197 万次引用。

研究在 ChatGPT、Google AI Mode 和 Google AI Overviews 中测试了这些搜索。

研究人员发现，大约有 116,000 个不同的域名被用作来源。

其中约 108,000 个是单个企业的网站，也就是约 93%。

当 BrightLocal 查看实际引用量时，单个企业的网站占近 200 万次引用的 42%——这仍然是一个很大的份额。

这也就是为什么完全专注于第三方平台的本地企业，可能会错过一部分机会。

是的，Google 商家资料很重要，评价很重要，Yelp 和相关目录网站很重要，第三方权威性也很重要。

不过，AI 系统也在从大量单个企业的网站获取信息。

这意味着，你的网站不仅是人们发现你之后才被引导去访问的地方，它还可以提供 AI 系统用来理解企业的第一方信息。

因此，你的网站应该让人能够非常容易地了解：

你是谁。

你做什么。

你在哪里经营。

你提供哪些服务。

你帮助哪些人。

在适当情况下，服务或产品的价格是多少。

客户会提出哪些问题。

以及如何联系你。

这些听起来很基础，但看看一般的本地企业网站：

一个首页。

一个关于我们页面。

一个联系表单。

可能还有一个笼统的服务页面。

然后就没有多少其他内容了。

这给 Google 和 AI 系统提供的第一方信息相对较少。

不妨换个场景想象：你在洛杉矶经营一家暖通空调公司。

你的网站清楚地涵盖空调维修、热泵、无风管系统、维护、定价问题、服务区域、常见问题，以及维修还是更换的决策。

这时，如果 AI 系统正在研究：

“帕萨迪纳维修热泵的最佳暖通空调公司”

或者：

“伯班克附近谁维修三菱分体式空调？”

它就有可能接触到多得多的相关第一方信息。

这就是机会所在。

[SEO Stuff Gold Plan Package](https://t.co/MMsDTFf4rg)

BrightLocal 的研究还发现了另一个值得注意的现象。

在 Google 地图上排名靠前，并**不会**自动转化为同等程度的 AI 可见度。

Google 地图在 66% 的搜索中提到了被追踪的企业。

Google AI Overviews：38%。

ChatGPT：33%。

Google AI Mode：32%。

因此，一家企业可以在地图中表现非常好，却仍然缺席大量 AI 生成的本地结果。

BrightLocal 发现，在研究中出现的企业里，Google AI Mode 与 AI Overviews 的重合率只有约 29%。

ChatGPT 与 Google 的任一 AI 结果界面的重合率只有约 19%—20%。

同一个本地市场，呈现出来的企业却可能截然不同。

你可能在 Google 地图上占据优势，在 ChatGPT 中却几乎不出现；在 AI Overviews 中出现得更频繁，到了 AI Mode 又消失了。

这就是为什么只在一个平台上检查一次是不够的，也说明 AI 搜索优化不应被视为本地 SEO 的替代品。

基础工作依然重要。

这组数据还有另一个有用的启示：单个企业的网站占被使用的**独立域名**的绝大多数，但大型平台仍然产生了巨大的引用量。

在 BrightLocal 对来源的分析中，Google 商家资料占约 29% 的引用。

Yelp 是另一个主要来源，尤其是在 ChatGPT 中。

本地 AI 搜索似乎依赖一个生态系统：你的网站、Google 商家资料、评价、目录网站、行业来源、本地出版物等。

你希望所有这些地方的信息都准确且一致。

不过，你最能控制的是自己的网站。网站需要提供足够的信息，让 AI 系统理解这家企业是否真正适合特定情境。

这适用于牙医、会计师、屋顶工、水管工、房地产经纪人、承包商、兽医、金融专业人士以及几乎所有其他本地企业。

客户的问题越具体，详细的第一方信息就可能越有用。

接下来还有权威性方面的工作。

你自己的网站只是本地搜索生态系统的一部分。

## 英文原文

If you run a local business, there is a big AI Search opportunity sitting on the website you already own.

A study analyzed more than 200,000 local AI searches and nearly 2 million citations.

The result?

93% of the *unique* domains AI systems used as sources were individual business websites, and business websites accounted for 42% of all citations.

So despite all the talk about Reddit, directories, review platforms and third-party sources, individual business websites still matter enormously in local AI Search.

Let's go through it.

By the way, if you want to see whether your business is appearing across Google AI, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Grok and broader AI search, start here. It's free:


https://
seo-stuff.com/free-audit

BrightLocal analyzed 200,875 non-branded local AI searches across 1,342 business locations, multiple checks over 60 days and roughly 1.97 million citations.

The searches were tested across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Google AI Overviews.

The researchers found roughly 116,000 unique domains being used as sources.

Around 108,000 were individual business websites, so approximately 93%.

When BrightLocal looked at actual citation volume, individual business websites accounted for 42% of the nearly 2 million citations - still a massive share.

And this is why local businesses focusing entirely on third-party platforms may be missing part of the opportunity.

Yes, Google Business Profile matters, reviews matter, Yelp and relevant directories matter, and third-part authority matters.

That said, AI systems are also drawing from a huge number of individual business websites.

That means your website is not simply somewhere you send people *after* they discover you, it can also provide first-party information AI systems use to understand the business.

So your website should make it extremely easy to understand:

Who you are.

What you do.

Where you operate.

Which services you provide.

Who you help.

What things cost when appropriate.

What questions customers ask.

And how somebody can contact you.

This sounds basic, but look at the average local business website.

A homepage.

An About page.

A contact form.

Maybe one generic Services page.

Then very little else.

That gives Google and AI systems relatively little first-party information to work with.

Imagine instead that you run an HVAC company in Los Angeles.

Your website clearly covers AC repair, heat pumps, ductless systems, maintenance, pricing questions, service areas, common problems and repair-vs-replacement decisions.

Now an AI system researching:

"Best HVAC company for a heat pump repair in Pasadena"

or:

"Who repairs Mitsubishi mini splits near Burbank?"

has considerably more relevant first-party information it can potentially encounter.

That is the opportunity.

The BrightLocal study found something else worth paying attention to.

Ranking well in Google Maps did NOT automatically translate into equivalent AI visibility.

Google Maps mentioned the tracked business in 66% of searches.

Google AI Overviews:38%.

ChatGPT: 33%.

Google AI Mode: 32%.

So a business can perform very well in Maps and still be missing from a huge portion of AI-generated local results.

BrightLocal found Google AI Mode and AI Overviews shared only about 29% of the businesses surfaced in the study.

ChatGPT overlapped with either Google AI surface only around 19-20%.

Same local market, but potentially very different businesses being surfaced.

You might dominate Google Maps, barely appear in ChatGPT, show up more frequently in AI Overviews and then disappear again in AI Mode.

That is why checking one platform once is not enough, and it is also why AI Search Optimization should not be treated as a replacement for local SEO.

The fundamentals still matter.

There is another useful lesson in the dataset: individual business websites made up the overwhelming majority of *unique* domains used, but large platforms still generated enormous citation volume.

Google Business Profile accounted for roughly 29% of citations in BrightLocal's source analysis.

Yelp was another major source, particularly for ChatGPT.

Local AI Search appears to rely on an ecosystem: your website, GBP, reviews, directories, industry sources, local publications, etc.

You want accurate, consistent information across all of them.

The one you have most control of, though, is your website. And it needs enough information for an AI system to understand whether the business actually fits that context.

This applies to dentists, accountants, roofers, plumbers, real estate agents, contractors, veterinarians, financial professionals and almost every other local business.

The more specific the customer's question becomes, the more useful detailed first-party information can become.
